condition: NSTEMI presenting as epigastric pain, first labelled gastritis
summary: 62-year-old diabetic man confirmed as gastritis; troponin returns at 480 ng/L.

inputs.hpi: Two hours of epigastric discomfort with nausea and sweating, started at rest. Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, smoker. Took antacids with no relief.

mustInclude.note: A raised high-sensitivity troponin with epigastric pain in a diabetic smoker is ACS until proven otherwise (ESC 2023).
mustInclude.knownGapNote: iOS (CI 2026-09-25 run 36200720842; simulator after the iOS parity port, 2026-09-26): no alert. Not the laboratory conversion: the 480 ng/L troponin becomes the 'elevated troponin' chip and fires ACS 'Raised or rising troponin' (database LR 8). The iOS database has no gastritis candidate, so the confirmed 'Gastritis' (K29.70) cannot be compared with the leader (the web compares it with PANE's gastritis node), and ACS reaches about 25-30 % on iOS (softmax over about 40 routed candidates; the core needs the leader >= 50 % and a finding with an LR ratio >= 10). The text parser's false peptic-ulcer evidence ('Took antacids with no relief' read as relief by antacids and as burning pain) is fixed, so ACS now leads the iOS differential. Needs a content decision (a gastritis candidate and / or graded troponin evidence above the ESC 0 h rule-in threshold): docs/clinical-validation/changes/diagnostic-reasoning.md, iOS parity.

guideline.name: ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes
guideline.citation: Byrne RA et al. Eur Heart J 2023;44:3720-3826

guideline.name: The importance of cognitive errors in diagnosis and strategies to minimize them

rationale: Epigastric pain labelled gastritis in a diabetic is a recognised trap; the troponin result must trigger the guard.
